activity_context.topic_title: Representing 2x2 Systems of Equations Using a Matrix Product

feedback.problem:
What is the system of equations represented by

$$
[\begin{aligned}8 & -4 \\ -6 & 12\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}16 \\ -18\end{aligned}]?
$$

The corresponding system of equations is

| { | {{field-1}} | $=$ | $\,4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-2}} | $=$ | $\,\,3.$ |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
The $2\times 2$ matrix encodes the coefficients of $x$ and $y$, and the $2\times 1$ vector on the right gives the constants, so the system is

$$
{\begin{aligned}8x-4y=16 \\ -6x+12y=-18\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the first equation by $4$ and the second by $-6$ gives the simplified system

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-y=4 \\ x-2y=3\end{aligned}
$$

which matches the entries shown above.
